note:
Joseph F Youngman, assistant bank manager, a single man keeping house with his elder sister and one young servant at 15 Park Terrace (#254) on the 1891 return, transcribed by A. Hagues. None of the three was in the record, and 15 Park Terrace held only 1921 (the Trumans), so 1891 is free.

**The directory keeps him at the house through the decade.** Wright's Directory of Nottingham prints 'Italian villas, Joseph F. Youngman, Bank clerk' at 15 Park Terrace in 1894-95 and 'Italian villas, Jph. F. Youngman, assistant manager of bank' there in 1898-99. The 1898-99 description matches this return exactly; the 1894-95 volume calls him a bank clerk, a step below what the census gives him three years earlier, and that difference is left standing rather than smoothed over. By 1910-11 number 15 belongs to James H. Soames and then to Mrs Betty Truman, which fits the Trumans being there in 1921.

**A probable later address, not joined here.** The same directories print 'Youngman Joseph Fletcher' at 38 The Ropewalk in 1910-11, 1913-14 and 1915-16. The distinctive name makes it very likely the same man, moved off Park Terrace, and it would give his middle name as Fletcher - but a directory line alone does not prove it, so nothing is added to his name and no Ropewalk address is recorded.

**'Italian villas' is a group name, not one house.** The 1898-99 volume prints it against numbers 15, 16 and 17 of Park Terrace, each with a different householder: Youngman at 15, William F. Bromley at 16, John Thompson Brewster at 17. None of the three properties (#254, #255, #256) carries a house name in the record, and this file does not set one, but the name looks worth adding to all three as a former group name.

Ages are as the enumerator wrote them, so a birth year worked back from one may be a year out either way.
source: 1891 census, 15 Park Terrace, transcribed by A. Hagues. Directory evidence: Wright's Directory of Nottingham 1894-95, page 107 (Leicester Special Collections id 164613); 1898-99, page 115 (id 165291).
